text: When an ECP5 NCO misses timing with an 18.06 ns BRAM-clock-to-out-to-unregistered-DSP path, shrink the table address to 6 bits and move the table from BRAM to LUT while adding pipeline registers (pipe_lut 0->2, pipe_mix 1->3, DSP in_pipe_out), raising Fmax from 55.37 to 115.34 MHz at +14 LUTs and unchanged DSP count by removing the BRAM read from the critical path and splitting the multiplier/post-multiplier carry chain.

On an ECP5 NCO at 115.3 MHz with pipe_mix=3 and a 6-bit LUT sine table, do not switch to a 10-bit BRAM table and drop to pipe_mix=2, because the BRAM clock-to-out (5.83 ns) plus carry chain becomes the limiter and Fmax falls to 106.2 MHz (-9.1) for only 14 LUTs saved; keep the LUT table or add a register immediately after the BRAM read.

When an ECP5 NCO timing path is limited by a 5.83 ns BRAM table read (SINE.0.0) feeding the DSP, move the sine table from BRAM to LUT and reduce the LUT address width 10->8, which removes the BRAM clock-to-out from the path and raises Fmax 106.2->114.4 MHz (+8.2 MHz) at +79 LUTs, leaving the DSP M->P/carry chain as the next limit.

When an ECP5 NCO mixer is timing-limited by the FF(x_l_q)->MULT18X18D->24-cell negate carry-chain path at ~8.73 ns, dropping LUT addr width from 8 to 6 and setting dsp_regs=in_pipe_out/out only saves 65 LUTs and leaves fmax at ~114.5 MHz, so instead force DSP output-register-only mode to make the P register launch the 24-bit negate and remove the 3.93 ns combinational A/B->P array from that cycle.

When an ECP5 NCO misses timing with an 18.06 ns BRAM-clock-to-out-to-unregistered-DSP path, shrink the table address to 6 bits and move the table from BRAM to LUT while adding pipeline registers (pipe_lut 0->2, pipe_mix 1->3, DSP in_pipe_out), raising Fmax from 55.37 to 115.34 MHz at +14 LUTs and unchanged DSP count by removing the BRAM read from the critical path and splitting the multiplier/post-multiplier carry chain.

When an ECP5 NCO is timing-limited at 115 MHz by a DSP→24-bit two's-complement product-negate carry chain, don't replace the 6-bit LUT sine table with a 10-bit BRAM table—it saves 14 LUTs but the 5.83 ns BRAM/select stage becomes critical and drops Fmax to 107 MHz—so keep the LUT table and pipeline the negate behind the DSP output register.

When an ECP5 NCO's BRAM sine table read dominates timing at 107 MHz (5.83 ns DP16KD logic fused with quadrant negate to 9.34 ns), move the table to LUTs with a 6-bit address and set dsp_regs to in_out so the DSP's P register launches the post-multiply negate/truncate carry chain, yielding 115.5 MHz (+8.4 MHz) at +14 LUTs and no DSP change.

When an ECP5 NCO is capped at 61 MHz by a 5.83 ns DP16KD BRAM table read feeding an unregistered MULT18X18D, move the table to a 6-bit quarter-wave LUT, add pipe_lut=2 registers after the read/negate, enable DSP in/out registers (in_pipe_out), and turn on dither, reaching 144 MHz (+83 MHz) at +26 LUTs and 0 extra DSPs by cutting the read-to-multiply-capture span from 16.33 ns to 6.92 ns.

On ECP5 NCO, when the critical path is FF(x_l_q) -> MULT18X18D -> FF(pq_m_q) at 144.5 MHz (already at the ~135 MHz 12x12 DSP array ceiling), setting dsp_regs=in_pipe_out,out does not insert a register before the multiplier's A/B inputs (path remains combinational), so fmax drops to 142.8 MHz (neutral); instead verify the input register is actually enabled rather than adding registers that leave the array in the cycle.

When an ECP5 NCO's critical path is FF→MULT18X18D→FF with 3.93 ns intrinsic DSP M→P delay and only ~1.3 ns route/setup slack, skip DSP input/output register packing (in_out, out) since it yields only +0.3 MHz—the MULT18X18D intrinsic delay is the fixed ceiling, so optimize the LUT/table path instead.

When an ECP5 NCO is pinned at ~143.1 MHz by the FF(x_l_q)→MULT18X18D→FF(pi_m_q) path (6.99 ns, of which 3.93 ns is DSP array logic and ~1.7 ns FF clk-to-Q/setup), adding mixed pipeline registers (pipe_mix 1→2, dsp_regs in_out/in_pipe_out) only reaches 144.3 MHz (+1.3 MHz, 0 LUT/DSP change) because no fabric register setting can shorten the 6.93 ns path already dominated by the intrinsic DSP array, so don't spend effort there—change the algorithm/table structure instead.

When an ECP5 NCO is timing-limited by the TRELLIS_FF→MULT18X18D→FF path at 144.3 MHz, avoid enabling DSP input-pipe plus output registers: doing so left LUT/DSP at 130/2 and dropped Fmax by 1.3 MHz to 143.1 MHz, because the 3.93 ns MULT18X18D array plus ~1.4 ns output route remains the bound.
